summary: Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1971. He taught at Komazawa University as a lecturer (~1978–1983) and later as Professor of Buddhist Studies (~1989–1997).

Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and he has taught Karl Brunnhölzl and Louise Child.

Rinzin Thargyal is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen, and later taught Palmo Kyi.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2004; she was at the University of Bristol in 2009.

Rita M. Gross worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning a degree at the University of Chicago (~1965–1975). She served as an assistant professor at UW-Madison (attested 1990) and was Professor Emerita of Philosophy and Religious Studies at UW-Eau Claire (~1979–2007).
Rizong Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama. In 1980, he served as abbot at Gyume Tantric College.

Rob Linrothe specializes in history/archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Minnesota, IUP, and Chicago (PhD ~1992), he held positions at Skidmore College (1992–2009), Northwestern University (2010–2022), the National Palace Museum (1986–1987), and the Rubin Museum of Art (2002–2004).

Rob Nairn is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of London, King's College London, and the University of Zimbabwe. He held academic posts at the University of Zimbabwe and the University of Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religion. After earning his PhD at Harvard (~1965–1972), he served as professor at Amherst College (1973, 1976) and director at Columbia University (1988).

Robert Aitken was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaii (~1947–1950), and Ryutaku-ji, and under D. T. Suzuki (~1957–1958). He held a post at the University of Hawaii.
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert B. Ekvall was a Tibetology scholar. He served as a research associate in anthropology at the University of Chicago, a research fellow and chairman at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (attested 1983).
Robert Barnett is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1973 to 1976. He subsequently served as a professor at Columbia University from circa 1998 to 2017.

Robert Caesar Childers studied at Wadham College (~1856–1860) and with Yataramulle Dhammarama (~1860–1864). Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, he held posts at the India Office (1872) and as Professor at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Oriel College from around 1877 to 1881 and later served as Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge, from circa 1924 to 1931.

Robert Chambers was an Indology scholar who studied at Lincoln College (~1754–1758). He held posts at the University of Oxford (~1766–1773), served as Chief Justice at Fort William (~1789–1798), and was president of the Asiatic Society (~1797–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner studied at Christ Church (~1933–1937) and worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Indology, and religion. He served in the Secret Intelligence Service (~1943–1952) and as Spalding Professor at the University of Oxford (~1952–1974).

Robert DeCaroli studied at UCLA (MA ~1995, PhD ~1999 under Robert L. Brown). Working in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held teaching posts at UCLA, Loyola Marymount, the Getty Research Institute, and George Mason University (faculty ~1999).

Robert Deliège is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford. He has held academic posts at the University of Kerala and as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (appointed around 1989).

Robert Duquenne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).
